title: Adaptive Test-Time Memory Allocation for Long-Tailed Human-Object Interaction Detection
abstract: arXiv:2511.18811v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Long-tailed human-object interaction (HOI) detection remains challenging because rare interactions are sparsely represented in training data. Although test observations provide additional visual evidence, existing cache-based methods typically assign uniform memory capacity across classes, limiting their ability to capture informative features of underrepresented interactions. To address this issue, we propose Adaptive Diversity Cache (ADC), a training-free, plug-and-play framework that adaptively constructs test-time caches through frequency-aware capacity allocation and confidence-diversity joint sample selection. Specifically, Frequency-Aware Cache Adaptation assigns larger capacities to underrepresented interactions using frequency-dependent priorities and a weighted logarithmic allocation objective, and fills remaining slots with selected augmented views. translated_title: 面向长尾人-物交互检测的自适应测试时内存分配
translated_abstract: 长尾人-物交互（HOI）检测仍然具有挑战性，因为稀有交互在训练数据中的表示十分稀疏。尽管测试阶段的观察可以提供额外的视觉证据，但现有的基于缓存的方法通常在各类之间分配统一的内存容量，这限制了其捕捉欠表示交互中有信息量特征的能力。为了解决这一问题，我们提出了自适应多样性缓存（ADC），这是一个无需训练、即插即用的框架，通过频率感知的容量分配和置信度-多样性联合样本选择来自适应地构建测试时缓存。具体而言，频率感知缓存适应利用频率相关的优先级和加权对数分配目标，为欠表示的交互分配更大的缓存容量，并用选定的增强视图填充剩余的缓存槽位。置信度-多样性联合缓存选择则进一步结合预测置信度与样本多样性（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 提出了一种无需训练、即插即用的自适应多样性缓存（ADC）框架，通过频率感知的缓存容量分配与置信度-多样性联合样本选择，自适应地构建测试时缓存，从而有效提升长尾人-物交互检测中稀有交互的识别性能。
en_tdlr: We propose Adaptive Diversity Cache (ADC), a training-free, plug-and-play framework that adaptively allocates test-time cache capacity based on class frequency and jointly selects samples by confidence and diversity, effectively improving detection of rare interactions in long-tailed human-object interaction detection.
